other_side: Where the edition treats Anthropic's trust problem as a delivery problem — promises not yet kept, fixable by curing cancer rather than by better messaging — Zitron reads the same week's news as a financing problem being dressed up as a narrative one. He goes straight at the two-trillion-dollar whisper number, calling the investor leak to the FT and the follow-up Reuters piece a pre-IPO marketing campaign rather than reporting, and objects that Anthropic is being priced on revenue it might book in two years while its actual losses go unmentioned. His sharpest line is aimed at the reasoning, not the company: valuing a business on what it could become is, he says, "a euphemism for 'ignore your lying eyes'." He also notes the same Gavin Baker "only companies" claim the episode covers, and treats it as evidence of how unmoored the discourse has become. On his account both frontier labs are unprofitable at scale, and the promises Dario concedes are undelivered are the collateral on which the whole valuation rests.
truth_beneath: Both men orbit the same variable: whether the frontier labs can convert their promises into money before the money runs out. They agree on more than the tone suggests — that the promises are so far undelivered, that Anthropic is growing fast, and that a two-trillion-dollar price implies profits nobody has yet shown. The empirical question is what an actual S-1 discloses, and the observable that settles it is audited revenue, gross margin and compute commitments in a filed prospectus rather than a leaked annualised run rate. Whittemore is vindicated if the filing shows real, diversified, improving-margin enterprise revenue and the medical results Dario promises in months arrive; Zitron if the numbers land closer to the losses he reconstructs and the IPO is delayed or repriced. Both are polemicists with incentives — Whittemore bullish and anti-doom, Zitron bubble-certain and anti-hype — and the signal is where they agree despite opposite priors: annualised run rates are marketing, and delivery is still owed. Watch for the S-1 itself, and for whether those "early glimmers" in biology are published or merely announced.
